heard: Emergency push bar doors were not designed for simple convenience. In 1883, over 1,100 children packed Victoria Hall in Sunderland. Free toys were promised, triggering a rush down the stairs. At the bottom, an inward door was bolted open one child wide. Trapped against it, 183 children suffocated in the stairs. The disaster forced new laws creating push bar emergency exits. Public safety doors were born from disaster, not convenience.
